qs.stem: How many different levels of heading does HTML support?
qs.sol:
The levels represent the importance and structural hierarchy of the content on a webpage:

<h1> : The most important heading. It is typically used for the main title of a page. Search engines and screen readers rely on this to understand the primary topic.

<h2>  through <h6> : These are used for sub-sections. As the number increases, the visual size of the text typically decreases, and the "importance" level drops.
qs.rel: Heading levels. Neighbours: h1 biggest/most important to h6 smallest; there is no h7; headings are block elements, used by search engines for structure; use title for page title, not h1 by default.

qs.stem:
Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements?
 i) Class is one of the HTML global attributes which specifies one or more class names for an element (refers to a class in a style sheet).
 ii) HTML is a markup language used for server-side processing.
 iii) CSS describes how HTML elements are to be displayed on screen, paper, or in other media.

- **HTML** = HyperText Markup Language; a **markup** (not programming) language, derived from **SGML**; **HTML5** = W3C Recommendation 2014. **Tag** = name in `< >`; **element** = start tag + content + end tag; **void/empty elements** have no end tag: `
`. **Attributes** are name="value" pairs, always in the **start tag**; **global attributes**: `id` (unique), `class`, `style`, `title`, `lang`, `hidden`, `tabindex`, `contenteditable`, `data-*`. - **Document skeleton:** `` (not a tag; selects HTML5 mode) -> `` -> `` (metadata: ``, `<meta charset="utf-8">`, `<meta name="viewport">`, `<link rel="stylesheet" href>`, `<style>`, `<script>`, `<base href target>`) -> `<body>`. `<title>` is inside head; shown on the tab and used by search engines. - **Text tags:** `<h1>`-`<h6>` (6 levels, h1 largest), `<p>`, `<br>`, `<hr>`, `<pre>` (preserves spaces), `<b>`/`<strong>` (bold/important), `<i>`/`<em>` (italic/emphasis), `<u>`, `<mark>`, `<small>`, `<del>`, `<ins>`, `<sub>` (H<sub>2</sub>O), `<sup>`, `<q>`, `<blockquote>`, `<code>`, `<abbr title>`, `<address>`, `<cite>`. - **Links & media:** `<a href="url" target="_blank">`; `target` values `_self _blank _parent _top`; `href="#id"` jumps within page; `mailto:` opens mail client. `<img src alt width height>` - `alt` is fallback/accessibility text; HTML5 adds `<audio controls>`, `<video controls>`, `<source>`, `<canvas>`, `<svg>`; `<iframe src>` embeds a page. **Image map:** `<img usemap="#m">` + `<map name="m">` + `<area shape="rect|circle|poly" coords href>`. - **Lists:** `<ul>` (bullets), `<ol>` (numbers; `type="1|A|a|I|i"`, `start`, `reversed`), `<li>`, `<dl>` + `<dt>` term + `<dd>` description. topics.title: 2. CSS — Styles, Selectors, Box Model, Properties
topics.theory:
- **Three ways to apply CSS:** **Inline** (`style` attribute), **Internal** (`<style>` in `<head>`), **External** (`<link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="x.css">` — change one file to restyle the whole site). "Out-line style" is not a method. `link` attributes: rel, type, href (**not `ref`**).
- **Box model (inside → out):** **Content**, Padding, Border, Margin. `margin` shorthand sets all four sides in one declaration.
- **Properties:** `word-spacing` (space between words), `font-weight` (boldness), `font-variant` (small-caps), `font-style`, `font-family`, `font-size`, `text-decoration` values: underline, **overline**, line-through, none; `background-color` accepts colour name, hex, rgb()/rgba(), hsl().
- **Selectors:** type/element (`p`), class (`.x`), id (`#x`), universal (`*`), grouping (list). 
- **Responsive web design** = HTML + CSS that automatically resizes a site for all devices. **Bootstrap** = most popular CSS framework for responsive, mobile-first sites; Tailwind CSS = utility-first framework.
- **Colour:** hsl hue 0–360 (0 red, 120 green, 240 blue).

topics.deep:
- **CSS** = Cascading Style Sheets; separates presentation from HTML structure; a rule = `selector { property: value; }` (declaration block of semicolon-separated declarations). Comment: `/* text */`.
- **Three ways to apply:** (1) **Inline** - `style="..."` attribute on one element (highest priority); (2) **Internal** - `<style>` block in `<head>` (one page); (3) **External** - separate `.css` file linked via `<link rel="stylesheet" href="a.css">` (one file restyles whole site; best for maintenance). `@import url()` is another way. A `<script>` is not a way to apply CSS. `!important` beats normal declarations.
- **Cascade & specificity:** order of precedence = importance, specificity, source order. Specificity weights: inline 1000, id 100, class/attribute/pseudo-class 10, element/pseudo-element 1; universal `*` = 0.
- **Selectors:** type/element `p`, class `.note`, id `#top`, universal `*`, group `h1, h2`, descendant `div p`, child `div > p`, adjacent sibling `h1 + p`, general sibling `h1 ~ p`, attribute `a[target="_blank"]`, pseudo-classes `:hover :active :visited :link :focus :first-child :nth-child(2) :not()`, pseudo-elements `::before ::after ::first-line ::first-letter`. Link order mnemonic: **LoVe HAte** (link, visited, hover, active).
- **Box model (inside out):** **content** -> **padding** -> **border** -> **margin**. `width` applies to content by default (`box-sizing: content-box`); `border-box` includes padding+border. Margin/padding shorthand: 1 value = all; 2 = top/bottom, left/right; 3 = top, left/right, bottom; 4 = **top right bottom left** (clockwise). Vertical margins of adjacent blocks **collapse**. Padding is inside the border and shows the background; margin is transparent.
- **Colour:** names, `#RRGGBB`, `#RGB` shorthand, `rgb(r,g,b)` 0-255, `rgba(...,a)`, `hsl(hue, sat%, light%)` with **hue 0-360 degrees** (0 red, 120 green, 240 blue), `hsla`. No binary notation. `transparent`, `currentColor`.
- **Background:** `background-color`, `-image: url()`, `-repeat` (repeat, no-repeat, repeat-x), `-position`, `-size` (cover, contain), `-attachment` (fixed, scroll).
- **Text:** `color`, `text-align` (left, right, center, justify), `text-decoration` (none, underline, overline, line-through), `text-transform` (uppercase, lowercase, capitalize), `text-indent`, `letter-spacing`, **`word-spacing`** (space between words), `line-height`, `white-space`, `text-shadow`.
- **Font:** `font-family` (list with generic fallback: serif, sans-serif, monospace), `font-size`, **`font-weight`** (normal, bold, 100-900), `font-style` (normal, italic, oblique), **`font-variant`** (normal, small-caps), shorthand `font: italic bold 12px/30px Arial`.
- **Units:** absolute `px, pt, cm, mm, in, pc`; relative `em` (font size of element/parent), `rem` (root), `%`, `vw`, `vh`. **Display:** `block, inline, inline-block, none` (removed from layout) vs `visibility:hidden` (space kept). **Position:** static (default), relative, absolute, fixed, sticky; `z-index`. **Float/clear**, **Flexbox** (`display:flex; justify-content; align-items; flex-direction`), **Grid** (`display:grid; grid-template-columns`).
- **Lists/tables:** `list-style` shorthand = type + position + image; `border-collapse: collapse`; `border: 1px solid black` (width style colour). `overflow: visible|hidden|scroll|auto`. `opacity: 0-1`. `cursor: pointer`.
- **Responsive & frameworks:** media query `@media (max-width: 600px) {...}`; `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`. **Bootstrap** (12-column grid, mobile-first, most popular); Tailwind = utility-first; Foundation, Bulma also exist. CSS3 adds rounded corners (`border-radius`), shadows, gradients, transitions, animations (`@keyframes`).
- **Likely question angles:** (1) `margin: 10px 20px 30px 40px` - which side gets what? (2) Order of box-model layers. (3) Specificity: which colour wins for id vs class vs element? (4) `display:none` vs `visibility:hidden`. (5) Identify `a:hover`, `p > span`, `#id`, `.class`. (6) Invalid value for `text-align`/`font-style`. (7) Effect of `text-transform: capitalize`. (8) Hue 120 in HSL is green. (9) Which `position` value is relative to the viewport (`fixed`)? (10) External vs internal vs inline CSS advantages.

topics.title: 3. JavaScript, DOM & jQuery
topics.theory:
- **JavaScript:** client-side scripting; extension **`.js`**; embedded with **`<script>` … `</script>`** (head or body, **unlimited** scripts); accepts **single, double and backtick quotes**; can change HTML content, attributes and **CSS styles**, hide/show elements; defines **behaviour/interactivity** (events). Web scripting = creating and embedding scripts in pages.
- **String + number:** `"Volvo"+16+4` = **"Volvo164"** (left-to-right concatenation); `16+4+"Volvo"` = "20Volvo".
- **DOM:** objects with properties, methods, events; **window** = top-level browser object (master container); **document** = holds the page content; `location` = URL; `alert()` shows dialog. **Methods = actions** performed on objects; properties = values.
- **Callback function** = function passed into another function as argument. **`instanceof`** → true if object is an instance of a type. **`for…in`** iterates object property keys. `event.preventDefault()` stops default action (e.g., form submit). `Object.defineProperty` with writable:false blocks assignment.
- **Events:** onchange, onmouseover, onkeydown, onload (page finished loading), onclick, onsubmit — events give a **dynamic** interface.
- **jQuery:** `hide()` and `show()` methods; `$("p").hide()`. DHTML = **Dynamic** HTML (HTML + CSS + JavaScript + DOM), not a language.

- **ASP objects:** **Response** (send output to user), Request (read client input), Session, Application (methods **Lock/Unlock**), Server. Server variable **HTTP_USER_AGENT** = browser description. **AdRotator** component shows a different image on each refresh.
- **VBScript:** single data type **Variant**; declare with **`Dim`**; assignment `strName = "John Smith"`; **`CSng`** converts to Single; **`Timer`** = seconds since 12:00 AM; **Sub procedure does not return a value (Function does)**; constants Empty, Nothing, Null.
- **ADO = ActiveX Data Objects**; **Connection object opens a connection to a data source**; Recordset holds records.
- **.NET:** **CLR (Common Language Runtime)** = virtual machine that manages execution (includes the JIT compiler); **WPF = Windows Presentation Foundation**; **data binding** connects data source to controls; **AJAX = Asynchronous JavaScript And XML** (update parts of a page without reload).
- **PHP:** open-source server-side scripting; uses **SQL commands** inside the script to store HTML form data in a database; MySQL back end.

qs.stem: Which ASP development model is successor to classic ASP?
qs.sol:
Concept: A server-side web framework processes browser requests on the server and generates responses such as HTML. A platform supplies the runtime and services; a development model specifies how an application organizes pages, events, or request handling.

To identify a successor, distinguish the historical replacement of a technology from particular programming models and later generations within its family.

Classic ASP executes server-side scripts embedded in pages. For example, a request for a page can execute VBScript, retrieve data, and return generated HTML.

Microsoft introduced ASP.NET as the succeeding web framework built on the .NET runtime. …
qs.rel: ASP successor. Neighbours: ASP.NET replaced classic ASP; compiled not interpreted; .aspx pages; Web Forms, MVC, Web API, Core; runs on CLR with languages like C# and VB.NET.

qs.stem: Which of the following is a valid assignment in ASP?
qs.sol: The print uses typographic quotes as stand-ins for code quotes. The intended executable VBScript form is strName="John Smith", with an assignable variable on the left.
qs.rel: VBScript assignment. Neighbours: VBScript uses = for assignment and comparison, & for concatenation, ' for comments, Set for object references (Set rs = ...), Dim for declaration, Option Explicit.

qs.stem: What is AJAX in ASP.NET?
qs.sol: AJAX is the abbreviation of Asynchronous JavaScript and XML. It allows a web page to communicate with the server asynchronously, so only the required part of the page can be updated instead of reloading the entire page. Therefore, the expansion is Asynchronous JavaScript and XML.
qs.rel: AJAX. Neighbours: AJAX = Asynchronous JavaScript and XML; XMLHttpRequest/fetch updates part of a page without reload; JSON now common; ASP.NET AJAX uses UpdatePanel and ScriptManager.

qs.stem: Which of the following ASP objects is used to send information to the user?
qs.sol:
Response sends output from the ASP server to the user.

Request reads information sent by the client.
qs.rel: ASP Response object. Neighbours: Response sends output (Write, Redirect, End, Cookies); Request reads input (Form, QueryString, Cookies, ServerVariables); Server, Session, Application manage environment/state.

qs.stem: What is the full form of ASP with reference to ASP.NET?
qs.sol: ASP expands to Active Server Pages, Microsoft’s server-side web technology name. ASP.NET follows that naming.
qs.rel: ASP full form. Neighbours: ASP = Active Server Pages (Microsoft, server-side, IIS); ASP.NET extends it; JSP = JavaServer Pages; PHP = PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor; CGI = Common Gateway Interface.

qs.stem: What is the name of the virtual machine component of Microsoft .NET Framework which manages the execution of .NET programs?
qs.sol:
The Common Language Runtime (CLR) is the managed execution engine of the .NET Framework — essentially a virtual machine that loads compiled Intermediate Language (IL) code, verifies type safety, applies Just-In-Time (JIT) compilation to native machine code, and manages memory (garbage collection), exception handling, and security while a program runs.

The question asks specifically which .NET Framework virtual-machine component manages the execution of .NET programs — that is exactly the CLR's role: it hosts and executes the managed code within a running .NET program, from loading through to completion. …
qs.rel: CLR. Neighbours: CLR manages execution, memory (garbage collection), type safety, security, exceptions; JIT compiles MSIL to native; CTS and CLS define types and language rules; FCL is the class library.

qs.stem: Which of the following ASP VB functions converts an expression to a variant of subtype single?
qs.sol:
Concept: A VBScript variable stores a Variant, whose subtype identifies how its current value is represented.

Explicit conversion functions select a numeric subtype. Single and Double use floating-point representations; Integer and Long use integral representations.

Application: In classic ASP, VBScript code runs on the server. The requested conversion must produce a Variant with the Single subtype.

Start with a numeric value such as 12.5, which has a fractional part.

Apply CSng(12.5): the value remains 12.5 and the result has subtype Single.

Inspect the result with TypeName(CSng(12.5)); it reports Single. Thus both the converted value and its subtype can be checked. …
qs.rel: VBScript conversion. Neighbours: CInt integer, CLng long, CSng single, CDbl double, CStr string, CBool Boolean, CDate date, CCur currency; Int/Fix truncate; Variant is the only type.

qs.stem: Which of the following keywords is used to explicitly declare variables in ASP?
qs.sol:
VBScript in ASP uses Dim to declare a variable.

Option Explicit requires declarations but is not itself the variable declaration keyword.
qs.rel: Dim keyword. Neighbours: Dim declares variables, ReDim resizes dynamic arrays, Const declares constants, Option Explicit forces declaration; variables are Variant; Private/Public set scope.

qs.stem: Which of the following is NOT a development model supported by ASP?
qs.sol:
The printed ASP.NET APT label does not name an ASP development model.

The other labels identify ASP or ASP.NET variants.
qs.rel: ASP.NET models. Neighbours: Web Forms (events, server controls), MVC (separates model/view/controller), Web Pages (Razor), Web API, Blazor; classic ASP is unrelated; Windows Forms is desktop.

qs.stem: Which of the following is NOT a built-in constant in ASP?
qs.sol:
Empty, Nothing, and NULL are recognised VBScript values or keywords used in ASP.

FULL is not a built-in constant.
qs.rel: VBScript constants. Neighbours: Empty (uninitialised), Null (no valid data), Nothing (no object), True/False, vbCrLf, vbTab; FULL is not a constant; IsEmpty/IsNull test them.

qs.stem: Which of the following is the expansion of ADO with respect to ASP?
qs.sol:
ADO expands to ActiveX Data Objects, the database access interface used with ASP.

ADO does not expand Alternative.
qs.rel: ADO. Neighbours: ADO = ActiveX Data Objects (Microsoft data access), built on OLE DB; ODBC is older; ADO.NET is the .NET version; objects Connection, Recordset, Command.

qs.stem: Which of the following should be placed inside PHP script to store information in the database through HTML form?
qs.sol: A PHP script uses SQL commands to insert form data into a database. The form supplies the data; the database operation is expressed as a query.
qs.rel: PHP and database. Neighbours: PHP runs SQL (INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE, DELETE) via mysqli/PDO; MySQL stores data; HTML forms send data through $_POST/$_GET; SQL injection is prevented by prepared statements.

qs.stem: Which of the following functions of ASP is used to get the number of seconds since 12:00 AM?
qs.sol:
Timer returns the number of seconds elapsed since midnight.

Time returns a time value, while TimeValue and TimeSerial create or convert time values.
qs.rel: Timer. Neighbours: Timer returns seconds since midnight; Now returns date and time; Date, Time; DateDiff, DateAdd, DatePart; Weekday, MonthName; Timer is often used to time code.

qs.stem: Which of the following data-types is supported by VBScript, which is often used to create ASP that can store different types of data?
qs.sol:
VBScript variables have the Variant data type, which can hold values of different subtypes.

The other terms describe values or subtypes, not its general variable type.
qs.rel: VBScript data type. Neighbours: only Variant, which holds subtypes Integer, String, Date, Boolean, Double, Empty, Null, Object; VarType and TypeName reveal the subtype.

qs.stem: The ADO connection object is used to:

opts.A: Hold a set of records from a database table
opts.B: Create an open connection to a data source
opts.D: Display only selected set of records and fields to view

qs.sol:
The ADO Connection opens a link to a data source.

Displaying Recordset data is separate from establishing a connection.
qs.rel: ADO Connection. Neighbours: Connection opens link to data source (Open, Execute, Close, BeginTrans), Recordset holds rows (MoveNext, EOF), Command runs parametrised queries.

qs.stem: The term ____ in ASP.NET means that data that is collected from a source is bound to the controls that provide the read and write connection to the data.
qs.sol:
In ASP.NET, Data binding refers to the process of connecting data from a data source to controls such as GridView, ListBox, or TextBox. These controls can then read, display, and sometimes update the data.

Data binding simplifies the interaction between the user interface and the data source.
qs.rel: Data binding. Neighbours: data binding connects UI controls (GridView, Repeater, DropDownList) to data sources using DataSource and DataBind(); ADO.NET provides data access; two-way binding in modern frameworks.

qs.stem: Which of the following ASP server variables returns a string that describes the browser that sent the request?
qs.sol:
HTTP_USER_AGENT carries the browser user-agent description from the request.

SERVER_NAME names the host serving the request.
qs.rel: Server variables. Neighbours: HTTP_USER_AGENT browser info, REMOTE_ADDR client IP, REQUEST_METHOD, QUERY_STRING, HTTP_REFERER, SERVER_NAME; accessed with Request.ServerVariables("name").

qs.stem: Which of the following is a method of ASP application object?
qs.sol:
Application.Lock is a method that prevents other sessions from changing application-wide variables during an update.

The other names belong to other members or objects.
qs.rel: Application object. Neighbours: Application.Lock/Unlock protect shared variables; Session.Timeout/Abandon; Response.Write; Request.Form; Application_OnStart in global.asa.

qs.stem: Which of the following is FALSE with respect to VBScript sub procedures in ASP?

opts.A: Sub procedure is a series of statements
opts.B: Sub procedure is enclosed by Sub and End Sub statements
opts.C: Sub procedure will perform actions and return a value

qs.sol:
A VBScript Sub executes statements but does not return a value.

A Function procedure can return a value.
qs.rel: Sub vs Function. Neighbours: Sub performs actions, no return value; Function returns a value by assigning to its name; both can take arguments; call Sub with Call or without parentheses.

qs.stem:
Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements?
 i) Just-In-Time compiler (JIT) is a part of Common Language Runtime (CLR).
 ii) .NET Framework is part of the .NET platform, a collection of technologies for building apps for Linux, macOS, Windows, iOS, Android.
 iii) ASP.NET applications are compiled codes, written using the extensible and reusable components or objects present in .NET framework.
qs.sol:
Statement (i) is true because the Just-In-Time compiler is a core component of the Common Language Runtime.

Statement (ii) is true as the .NET Framework supports cross-platform development within the broader .NET ecosystem. Statement (iii) is also true since ASP.NET applications utilize reusable components and compile to Intermediate Language code.
qs.rel: CLR and .NET. Neighbours: JIT is part of CLR; .NET (Core) is cross-platform, .NET Framework is Windows only; ASP.NET code is compiled to MSIL then JIT native; assemblies .dll/.exe.

qs.stem: Which of the following ASP component creates an object that displays a different image each time a user enters or refreshes a page?
qs.sol:
AdRotator selects and displays an advertisement image when the page is served.

Counter counts events; it does not select an image.
qs.rel: AdRotator. Neighbours: AdRotator shows a different ad on each page load based on XML schedule file; other components: Browser Capabilities, Content Rotator, Counters, FileSystemObject.

qs.stem: What does WPF stand for in the Microsoft .NET ecosystem?
qs.sol:
An acronym-expansion question is answered by matching the acronym to its officially documented name, not by picking a plausible-sounding phrase. Microsoft's .NET platform is made up of several named subsystems -- for example ASP.NET for web applications, WinForms for legacy desktop UI, and WPF for modern desktop UI -- each with a specific, vendor-documented full name.

WPF was introduced by Microsoft with .NET Framework 3.0 in 2006 as the subsystem for building rich Windows desktop applications using XAML markup, vector graphics, data binding, styles, and templates. Microsoft's own documentation (Microsoft Learn / .NET docs) records its full name as Windows Presentation Foundation. …
qs.rel: WPF. Neighbours: WPF = Windows Presentation Foundation (XAML desktop UI); WCF = Windows Communication Foundation; WF = Workflow Foundation; Silverlight, ADO.NET; CardSpace.

qs.stem: Which of the following is true with respect to ASP?

opts.A: Most of the functionality that can be built into ASP pages comes from objects on the client
opts.C: ASP enables client side scripting for IIS
opts.D: Files created with ASP have the extension .aspn

qs.sol:
Classic ASP can use more than one scripting language, so its technology is language-independent.

It executes server-side and normally uses the .asp extension.
qs.rel: ASP features. Neighbours: classic ASP is server-side, language-independent (VBScript default, JScript), runs on IIS, extension .asp; client-side scripting is JavaScript.

qs.stem: Which programming language is often used for server-side web development?
qs.sol:
PHP is a popular server-side scripting language widely used for web development. It executes on the web server and is mainly used to create dynamic web pages, manage databases, process forms, and handle user sessions.

For example:

WordPress is built using PHP.

PHP can interact with databases like MySQL.

HTML and CSS are used for webpage structure and styling, while JavaScript is mainly used for client-side scripting.

Therefore, PHP is commonly used for server-side web development.

qs.stem: Which scripting executes on the server before the page is sent to the browser?
qs.sol:
Correct Answer: C. Server-side scripting / सर्वर-साइड स्क्रिप्टिंग

Explanation (English):
Server-side scripting runs on the web server before the webpage is sent to the user's browser. It is used for tasks like database interaction, authentication, and dynamic content generation. Examples include PHP, Python, and Node.js.

qs.sol: In classic  Active Server Pages (ASP) ,  VBScript  is the default scripting language used for server-side scripting, although other languages like JavaScript can also be used.

qs.sol: An abstract method has a declaration but no body in its base class. A concrete derived class must implement that declared operation; ordinary virtual, sealed and static methods do not meet both conditions.

The  Enable property  is used to return or set a Boolean value that determines whether a control can respond to user-generated events.
 When true: the control can receive focus and respond to user input and events.

When false: the control is disabled, cannot receive focus, and will not respond to user actions.

qs.stem: When an ASP.NET file is placed on an IIS server and viewed through a browser, the resulting HTML page contains:

opts.A: a mix of ASP.NET and HTML code
opts.D: as much ASP.NET code as is in the ASP.NET file

qs.sol:
In ASP.NET, a request for an .aspx file is handled entirely on the server: IIS's ASP.NET runtime processes the file's server-side portions as part of handling that request, and the response it builds is based on what that processing produces. A server-side technology never ships its own source instructions to the client -- only whatever markup that processing yields becomes part of the response.

For the .aspx file hosted on this IIS server, a request triggers the ASP.NET engine to run the page's server-side logic relevant to that request (loops, conditionals, data binding, etc.) and produce the corresponding tags. …

topics.deep:
- **Server-side vs client-side:** server-side code (ASP, ASP.NET, PHP, JSP, Node) runs on the web server and only its HTML output reaches the browser (user cannot see the source code); client-side (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) runs in the browser. Server-side scripting gives dynamic pages, database access, security, session handling.
- **Classic ASP:** **Active Server Pages**, Microsoft, runs on **IIS** (Internet Information Services); extension **`.asp`**; script delimiters `<% ... %>`; **language-independent** - default VBScript, also JScript; `<%= expr %>` is shorthand for Response.Write. Comment in VBScript: `'` or `Rem`.
- **ASP built-in objects:** **Request** (gets data from client: `Request.QueryString`, `Request.Form`, `Request.Cookies`, `Request.ServerVariables`), **Response** (sends output to user: `Write`, `Redirect`, `End`, `Cookies`, `Buffer`), **Server** (`CreateObject`, `MapPath`, `HTMLEncode`, `URLEncode`, `ScriptTimeout`), **Session** (per user: `Session("x")`, `Timeout`, `Abandon`, `SessionID`), **Application** (shared by all users: `Lock`, `Unlock`, `Contents`). Events in **global.asa**: `Application_OnStart/OnEnd`, `Session_OnStart/OnEnd`. `Application.Lock` stops others changing shared variables during an update; `Timeout` belongs to Session; `Write` to Response; `Form` to Request.
- **ServerVariables:** `HTTP_USER_AGENT` (browser info), `REMOTE_ADDR` (client IP), `REQUEST_METHOD`, `QUERY_STRING`, `SERVER_NAME`, `HTTP_REFERER`.
- **ASP components:** **AdRotator** (shows a different banner/image on each visit/refresh, uses a schedule file), **Browser Capabilities**, **Content Rotator**, **Counters**, **File Access / FileSystemObject**, **Content Linking**.
- **VBScript basics:** one data type, **Variant**, holding subtypes (Empty, Null, Integer, Long, Single, Double, Currency, Date, String, Object, Boolean, Byte). Declare with **`Dim`** (also `Private`, `Public`, `ReDim`, `Const`); `Option Explicit` forces declaration. Constants/values: `Empty`, `Null`, `Nothing`, `True`, `False`, `vbCrLf`. Conversion functions: `CInt` (Integer), `CLng`, `CSng` (Single), `CDbl` (Double), `CStr`, `CBool`, `CDate`, `CCur`. Others: `Len, Left, Right, Mid, UCase, LCase, Trim, InStr, Replace, Now, Date, Time`, **`Timer`** (seconds since midnight 12:00 AM), `IsNumeric, IsEmpty, IsNull`. Operators: `&` string concat, `\` integer division, `Mod`, `^`, `And Or Not`, `=` for equality and assignment, `<>` not equal.
- **Procedures:** **Sub** ... `End Sub` performs actions and **does not return a value**, can take arguments; **Function** ... `End Function` **returns a value** by assigning to the function name. Control: `If..Then..ElseIf..Else..End If`, `Select Case`, `For..Next` (`Step`), `For Each`, `Do While/Until..Loop`, `While..Wend`.
- **ADO (ActiveX Data Objects):** access databases from ASP. Objects: **Connection** (opens a link to a data source: `Server.CreateObject("ADODB.Connection")`, `.Open`, `.Execute`, `.Close`), **Recordset** (`MoveNext`, `EOF`, `BOF`, `Fields`, `AddNew`, `Update`), **Command**. Typical flow: create connection -> open -> execute SQL -> loop `Do While Not rs.EOF` -> close.
- **ASP.NET:** successor to classic ASP; **compiled** code, event-driven, extension `.aspx`, code-behind `.cs/.vb`; runs on the **.NET Framework** with **CLR** (Common Language Runtime = the virtual-machine component that manages execution, memory/garbage collection, security; contains the **JIT** compiler turning MSIL into native code) and the class library. Languages: C#, VB.NET. Development models: **Web Forms**, **MVC**, **Web Pages** (Razor), Web API. **Data binding** = binding controls (GridView, DropDownList) to a data source. **WPF** = Windows Presentation Foundation (desktop UI, XAML), **WCF** = Windows Communication Foundation. **ASP.NET AJAX** = Asynchronous JavaScript and XML (UpdatePanel, ScriptManager).
- **PHP:** open-source server-side language, `<?php ... ?>`, ext `.php`, variables start with `$`, `echo`; commonly with **MySQL** (`mysqli_connect`, `mysqli_query`) running **SQL** commands (INSERT, SELECT) from the script to store data; `$_GET`, `$_POST`, `$_SESSION`; LAMP/XAMPP stack.
- **Likely question angles:** (1) Which function converts to Double/Long/String (`CDbl, CLng, CStr`)? (2) `Response.Write(5 & 3)` -> 53 but `5 + 3` -> 8. (3) Session vs Application scope. (4) Sub vs Function. (5) Which ADO object holds query results (Recordset)? (6) Expansion of CLR, JIT, MSIL, WCF, WPF, ADO, ODBC, IIS. (7) Where Session_OnStart lives (global.asa). (8) `Request.Form` (POST) vs `Request.QueryString` (URL). (9) Extensions .asp/.aspx/.php/.jsp. (10) Which component rotates ads (AdRotator)?

topics.title: 6. E-commerce & E-business
topics.theory:
- **EDI** = Electronic Data Interchange; **EFT** = Electronic Fund Transfer; **EPS** types: smart cards, e-wallet, EFT, credit/debit cards. **M-commerce:** mobile security is a major impediment; reduces transaction cost; mobile payments/coupons.
- **Advantages of e-commerce:** reduced paperwork and cost, 24×7 availability, wider reach; **user resistance is a challenge, not an advantage.** Key drivers of e-business: commercial benefits, customers'/suppliers' requirements, skilled and committed workforce (not "supplementary workforce").
- **Online trading steps:** open Demat + trading account → allocate funds → place order → system forwards to exchange. **Barriers** external to organisation (micro-environment): business models etc. **Visibility strategies:** guessable sensible domain name, upload special offers/content regularly.

qs.stem: With respect to e-commerce, what is the full form of EFT?
qs.sol: EFT stands for Electronic Fund Transfer. It means transferring money electronically from one account or system to another.
qs.rel: EFT. Neighbours: EFT covers NEFT (batch), RTGS (real-time, large values), IMPS (instant 24x7), UPI; EFT removes paper cheques; ECS, ACH are bulk transfers.

qs.stem: With respect to e-commerce, what is the full form of EDI?
qs.sol: EDI stands for Electronic Data Interchange. It is the computer-to-computer exchange of business documents in a standard electronic format.
qs.rel: EDI. Neighbours: EDI exchanges standard business documents computer-to-computer (invoices, POs) using ANSI X12 or EDIFACT; mainly B2B; reduces paperwork and errors; uses VANs historically.

qs.stem:
Which of the following are the types of Electronic Payment Systems (EPS)?
 I.  Smart Cards
 II.  E-Wallet
 III.  Electronic Funds Transfer
qs.sol: Smart cards, e-wallets and Electronic Funds Transfer are all examples of electronic payment systems.
qs.rel: EPS types. Neighbours: smart cards, e-wallets, EFT, credit/debit cards, net banking, UPI, digital cash; payment gateway connects merchant and bank; SSL/TLS secures transmission.

qs.stem: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of e-commerce?
qs.sol: Reduced paperwork, lower cost and 24x7 availability are advantages of e-commerce. User resistance is a challenge, not an advantage.
qs.rel: E-commerce disadvantages. Neighbours: advantages are 24x7, lower cost, less paperwork, global reach; limitations are security risk, no physical touch, internet dependence, delivery delays, fraud and trust issues.

qs.stem: Procedure for online trading involve(s) which of the following step(s)? I. Make an application to open a Demat Account and Online Trading Account. II. Allocate funds from the bank account to the trading account. III. Once the order is confirmed, it is placed in the stock exchange through the online trading system.
qs.sol: Online trading starts by opening Demat and trading accounts, then allocating funds. After an order is confirmed, the online system forwards it to the exchange. All three stated steps belong to the procedure.
qs.rel: Online trading. Neighbours: Demat (electronic shares, NSDL/CDSL), trading account, linked bank account, order placement via broker to NSE/BSE, SEBI regulator; settlement T+1; brokerage.

qs.stem: Which of the following is NOT a key driver of e-business?
qs.sol: A “key driver” of e-business is an internal, organisational-level force that pushes a firm to adopt and invest in electronic ways of doing business. Standard e-business frameworks group these drivers into a small, well-defined set: commercial benefit (cost and efficiency gains), a workforce that is skilled and committed to using the new technology, and the changing requirements of customers and suppliers who increasingly expect to transact online. …
qs.rel: E-business drivers. Neighbours: drivers include commercial benefits, customer/supplier pressure, skilled committed workforce, technology; external pressures vs internal capacity; barriers differ from drivers.

qs.stem:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct regarding m-commerce?
 I. Mobile security is one of the prominent impediments of m-commerce.
 II. M-commerce reduces overall transaction cost through streamlined business processes.
 III. Mobile coupons and mobile ticket delivery are m-commerce services.
qs.sol: Mobile security, reduced transaction cost, and mobile coupons/payments are all associated with m-commerce.
qs.rel: m-commerce. Neighbours: m-commerce = commerce via mobile devices; services like mobile banking, coupons, ticketing, mobile wallets; challenges security and small screen; uses WAP, 4G/5G, NFC.

qs.stem:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct regarding the strategies required to increase the visibility of e-commerce website?

I. The website name should be sensible that it can be guessed.

II. Uploading contents like special offers or eye catching information for the regular followers can increase traffic on the website.

III. Icons of social networks on the website have no major influence on e-visibility.
qs.sol: Statement I is correct because a meaningful and easy-to-guess website name improves recall and helps users find the site again. Statement II is also correct because regularly uploading special offers, useful information, or eye-catching content can increase repeat visits and website traffic. Statement III is incorrect because social-network icons or links can help users share the website and can bring traffic from social platforms. Therefore, only statements I and II are correct.
qs.rel: Website visibility. Neighbours: SEO, meaningful domain, fresh content/offers, social media links, backlinks, keywords, mobile friendliness all raise traffic; social icons do help.

qs.stem: Which of the following is a barrier to e-commerce related to micro-environmental issues external to the organisation?
qs.sol:
E-commerce barriers are grouped by where they arise relative to the organisation: internal barriers come from within the organisation's own resources and processes; external micro-environmental barriers come from the immediate market and industry context around the organisation, such as the practices of trading partners and competitors; external macro-environmental barriers come from the broader societal, technological, and cultural forces shaping the whole industry.

Among the options here, business models are the one rooted in the external market and industry context surrounding the organisation, which is exactly what defines a micro-environmental barrier. …
qs.rel: E-commerce barriers. Neighbours: internal (lack of experts, culture, resources), external micro (business models, customers, suppliers, competitors), macro (internet infrastructure, law, economy, tax).

qs.stem: During E‐commerce transaction we should ensure‐‐‐‐‐‐‐‐‐‐‐‐‐
qs.sol: An e-commerce transaction needs integrity to prevent unauthorized changes, confidentiality to protect sensitive information, and overall security controls to protect parties and the transaction. The combined requirement includes every listed property.

Modified from the official paper: the printed stem uses “E commerce” and a fragmented dash blank; the bank regularizes them as “E‐commerce” and a continuous blank. The meaning and marked answer are unchanged. An electronic transaction needs integrity against alteration, confidentiality against disclosure, and broader security controls such as authentication and access protection.

qs.stem: In EDI, I stands for?
qs.sol:
Concept: EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) is a standard for the direct, structured electronic exchange of business documents between the computer systems of two separate trading partners, replacing paper-based communication. Each letter of the acronym names one part of this definition: Electronic (the medium), Data (the structured business content), and Interchange (the fact that the data moves between two independent systems).

Application: In the acronym EDI, the letter I expands to Interchange, capturing the idea that structured data passes between two separate computer systems rather than staying within one. …

qs.stem: Digital Signature is a________?

opts.A: Digital id,send as an attachment to a web page/e‐mail/message
opts.B: Is used for verifying the attachments send using web
opts.C: Both "Digital id,send as an attachment to a web page/e‐mail/message" and "Is used for verifying the attachments send using web"

qs.sol:
A digital signature is a cryptographic value attached to digital content to authenticate its signer and integrity. The listed descriptions both attempt to capture this attachment and verification use, so the combined statement is the intended key. Answer as per the BSEB candidate response sheet (Correct Answer field), 11 Jun 2024 Shift 1 (code 203).
Answer as per the BSEB candidate response sheet (Correct Answer field), 2024-06-11-s1.

qs.stem: Which type of e‐commerce focuses on consumers dealing with each other?
qs.sol: Consumer-to-consumer commerce occurs when individuals trade directly with other individuals, usually through a marketplace. The other abbreviations identify business sellers or business buyers.

qs.stem: Which term specifically describes conducting business electronically?
qs.sol: Modified from the official paper: specified electronic conduct and replaced the overlapping “All of the above” choice with “None of the above”. E-commerce means business conducted electronically; general business and sale of goods can occur offline.

qs.sol: An electronic payment system provides the infrastructure that carries and processes online payments. EFT is a particular transfer mechanism and PayPal is one provider, so the sheet's broad EPS term is intended.

qs.sol: XML is used to store and transport data; it focuses on data representation and transfer, not on presentation or design.

qs.stem: A combination of software and information designed to provide security and information for payment is called a what?
qs.sol: A digital wallet stores payment credentials or value and presents them for an online transaction. That combined software-and-information role matches the description.

qs.stem: Which form of e‐marketplace brings together buyers and sellers from the same industry?
qs.sol: A vertical electronic marketplace concentrates on one industry and connects buyers and suppliers in that industry. A horizontal marketplace instead spans multiple industries.

topics.deep:
- **E-commerce** = buying/selling of goods, services and information over the internet/electronic networks. **E-business** is broader: all business processes (buying, selling, supply chain, customer service, collaboration with partners, internal operations) done electronically; e-commerce is a subset of e-business. **M-commerce** = commerce through mobile devices (smartphones, tablets) over wireless networks.
- **Business models by participants:** **B2B** (business to business - e.g. manufacturer to wholesaler, supplier portals, EDI), **B2C** (business to consumer - Amazon, Flipkart retail), **C2C** (consumer to consumer - OLX, eBay, classifieds, auctions), **C2B** (consumer to business - freelance, reverse auctions), **G2C / G2B / G2G** (e-governance: tax filing, tenders, passport), **B2E** (business to employee). Revenue models: advertising, subscription, commission/brokerage, affiliate, direct sales.
- **Advantages:** 24x7 availability, global reach, lower cost, reduced paperwork, faster transactions, wider choice, price comparison, reduced inventory. **Limitations:** security and privacy risk, no physical inspection, dependence on internet/infrastructure, delivery delays, fraud, legal/tax issues, trust.
- **Key drivers of e-business:** commercial benefits (cost, speed, competition), requirements/pressure of customers and suppliers, skilled and committed workforce, technology, government support. **Barriers** are internal (lack of skilled staff/experts, culture) versus external micro-environment (customers, suppliers, competitors, business models) and macro-environment (internet infrastructure, law, economy, taxation).
- **Visibility/traffic strategies:** meaningful, easily guessable domain name; search-engine optimisation (SEO); fresh content and special offers; social-network icons/sharing; email marketing; directory listings; banner ads; mobile friendly, fast site.
- **Electronic Payment Systems (EPS):** **credit card** (pay later), **debit card** (pay from account), **smart card** (chip card holding data/value), **e-wallet / digital wallet** (Paytm, PhonePe), **EFT** = Electronic Fund Transfer (NEFT - batch; RTGS - real-time gross settlement for large values; IMPS - instant 24x7; **UPI** - Unified Payments Interface by NPCI), **net banking**, **e-cheque**, **digital cash**. A payment gateway (e.g. Razorpay, CCAvenue) authorises payments between merchant and bank; security via SSL/TLS (https), OTP, two-factor authentication, digital signature, encryption, **SET** (Secure Electronic Transaction).
- **EDI** = Electronic Data Interchange: computer-to-computer exchange of standard-format business documents (purchase orders, invoices) between organisations without paper; standards ANSI X12 and UN **EDIFACT**; mainly B2B.
- **Online trading (stock market):** open a **Demat** account (shares in electronic form with depository NSDL/CDSL) plus a **trading account** with a broker, linked to a bank account; transfer funds to the trading account; place buy/sell order online; the confirmed order is routed to the exchange (NSE/BSE); regulator **SEBI**.
- **Related terms:** IT Act 2000 (India) gives legal recognition to electronic records and digital signatures; Certifying Authority issues digital certificates; SCM (supply chain), CRM, ERP, shopping cart, e-procurement, drop-shipping, COD (cash on delivery).
- **Likely question angles:** (1) Classify an example as B2B/B2C/C2C/G2C. (2) Full forms: EFT, EDI, NEFT, RTGS, UPI, SET, SSL, COD, SCM. (3) Which is NOT an EPS? (4) E-commerce vs e-business. (5) Advantage vs limitation of e-commerce. (6) Internal vs external barrier. (7) Steps in online trading. (8) Security method for payments (SSL, digital certificate). (9) m-commerce services (mobile banking, coupons, ticketing). (10) Which standard does EDI use?

topics.title: 7. Internet, Browsers, Web Concepts & Web Design
topics.theory:
- **WWW:** system of linked documents/resources accessed over the Internet using a browser; **website = collection of web pages**; webserver hosts them. **Web browser = client**; webmaster runs the web servers.
- **URI** names/identifies a resource; **URL** gives its location (a URL is a type of URI). **ARPA(NET)** funded 1960s research connecting computers. **BOOTP** = protocol for booting computers from the network (basis of DHCP). **Chrome DevTools: Ctrl+Shift+I** (Windows) — inspect/debug pages. **Geolocation** lets users share location with trusted sites.
- **Instant messaging:** Snapchat, WeChat, Signal (Firefox is a browser). Privacy concern: data security. Google Meet = video conferencing. Netiquette: proper grammar/punctuation, respectful posts.
- **Web design:** **wireframe** = rough skeletal outline (which content on which page, navigation between pages); tools: Webflow etc. User-friendly site: fast, accessible, browser-consistent, **not cluttered**. Static site: same content each load, no server-side processing, fast; dynamic: content changes.
- **Client-server:** client handles presentation, processing logic; shared resources are controlled by the server. Applet = Java program embedded in HTML. Front-end: HTML5 (markup), JS libraries (React), frameworks (Tailwind/Bootstrap), assets (Font Awesome), reset CSS (boilerplate).
- **Sequence structure:** statements execute in written order, once each, none repeated.

qs.stem: Which of the following features is provided by Google Meet?
qs.sol: Google Meet connects participants in real-time audio and video meetings. Video conferencing is its core function.
qs.rel: Video-conferencing tools. Neighbours: Google Meet vs Zoom vs MS Teams vs Skype; features like screen share, live captions, recording; Google Meet is part of Google Workspace and runs in a browser without install.

qs.stem: A collection of web pages is known as _____.
qs.sol: A collection of related web pages is called a website.
qs.rel: Website vs web page. Neighbours: web page = single document, home page = entry page, web server hosts the site, portal = site aggregating services. Domain name plus hosting is required to publish a site.

qs.stem: In DHTML, the letter 'D' stands for:
qs.sol: DHTML stands for Dynamic HTML. It is not a single language but a combination of technologies including HTML, CSS, and JavaScript that allows web pages to change dynamically without reloading.
qs.rel: DHTML. Neighbours: DHTML = HTML + CSS + JavaScript + DOM; it is a technique/combination, not a language; AJAX and jQuery build on it; DOM lets scripts change content and style after load.

qs.stem: What is the primary function of the World Wide Web (WWW)?

opts.A: To connect and access documents and resources over the internet

qs.sol: The World Wide Web links documents and other resources through network protocols. A browser requests a resource using its address, and the server returns the associated content. This lets users connect to and access documents and resources across the internet.
qs.rel: Purpose of the Web. Neighbours: Web = information system of linked hypertext documents over the Internet; invented by Tim Berners-Lee; accessed through HTTP and browsers; Internet is the network, Web is one service.

qs.stem: Which of the following is NOT an instant messaging service?
qs.sol: Firefox is a web browser. Snapchat, WeChat, and Signal support direct person-to-person messaging, so Firefox is the item outside that service category.
qs.rel: Messaging vs browsers. Neighbours: IM apps WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, WeChat, Snapchat; browsers Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, Opera; do not confuse application type with brand.

qs.stem: Which of the following is an application of the World Wide Web?

opts.B: Sending emails directly to a mobile phone
opts.C: Browsing websites and accessing online services

qs.sol: The World Wide Web is a system of linked resources accessed over web protocols. A browser lets users visit sites and use online services built on it.
qs.rel: Web applications. Neighbours: e-mail, e-commerce, e-learning, online banking, social networking, search are Web/Internet services; compare with desktop apps and offline tools like word processors.

qs.stem: Which of the following is a privacy concern with Instant Messaging (IM) applications?
qs.sol:
IM services transmit personal conversations and files, so unauthorized access or weak protection can expose private data.

Data security directly addresses confidentiality and protection of those communications.
qs.rel: IM privacy. Neighbours: risks are interception, stored chat logs, phishing links, identity exposure; mitigation is end-to-end encryption, strong passwords, 2FA; compare with email spam and cookies tracking.

qs.stem: Shortcut key used to open Google chrome developer tools in windows is ______.
qs.sol: In Chrome on Windows, the keyboard shortcut for opening Developer Tools is Ctrl+Shift+I. The extra Shift modifier distinguishes it from ordinary browser commands.
qs.rel: Developer tools shortcut. Neighbours: F12 or Ctrl+Shift+I opens DevTools; Ctrl+Shift+J console; Ctrl+U view source; Ctrl+Shift+Delete clear data; Ctrl+Shift+N incognito; Ctrl+Shift+T reopen tab.

qs.stem: Which of the following agency started showing interest, in 1960s, in finding a way to connect computers so that researchers could share their ideas?
qs.sol:
ARPA sponsored the early research that connected computers and enabled researchers to share information. This work led to ARPANET.

ARPA funded the early computer networking effort.
qs.rel: Origin of Internet. Neighbours: ARPA (US DoD) funded ARPANET (1969); packet switching; NSFNET; TCP/IP adopted 1983; Tim Berners-Lee invented WWW 1989-91 at CERN; Mosaic first popular browser.

qs.stem: Using HTML and CSS to automatically resize a website and making a website look good on all devices (desktops, tablets, and phones) is referred to as
qs.sol:
Responsive web design adapts a page layout to different screen sizes.

HTML and CSS can make it display well on desktops, tablets, and phones.
qs.rel: Responsive design. Neighbours: fluid grids, flexible images, CSS media queries, viewport meta tag; mobile-first; Bootstrap grid; adaptive design uses fixed layouts per device size.

qs.stem: _____ lets users show their location with websites they trust.
qs.sol:
Modern web browsers expose a permission-gated location mechanism: it determines a device's approximate physical position — via GPS, Wi-Fi access points, cell towers, or IP address — and hands those coordinates to a requesting website, but only after the user explicitly grants consent. This is what lets a user choose to reveal their location to sites they trust while keeping it hidden from everyone else.

This exact permission-based location-sharing mechanism is what browsers standardize as Geolocation (the Geolocation API), so the blank is filled by Geolocation. …
qs.rel: Geolocation. Neighbours: Geolocation API (navigator.geolocation) needs user permission, uses GPS, Wi-Fi, IP; works only on secure contexts (HTTPS); other permissions: camera, microphone, notifications.

qs.stem: ______ protocol is used for starting computers from the network.
qs.sol: Modified from the official paper: The official paper cancelled the item. BOOTP supplies boot-time network configuration to a diskless client.
qs.rel: Network boot protocol. Neighbours: BOOTP gives diskless clients IP and boot file; DHCP is its successor and also leases IPs; TFTP transfers boot image; ARP maps IP to MAC, RARP does reverse; DNS maps names to IPs.

qs.stem: What is the purpose of a web browser's developer tools?

opts.A: To inspect and debug web pages
opts.C: To host web pages on the web server

qs.sol:
Developer tools provide inspectors, consoles, debuggers, and network panels.

These functions let a developer inspect and debug a web page while it is loaded in the browser.
qs.rel: DevTools. Neighbours: Elements (DOM/CSS inspector), Console (JS errors, log), Network (requests, timings), Sources (debugger breakpoints), Application (cookies, storage), Lighthouse (performance audit).

qs.stem: A web browser is an example of ____.
qs.sol: A web browser acts as a client in the client-server model because it requests resources from web servers.
qs.rel: Client-server. Neighbours: browser = client, web server = server; client requests, server responds via HTTP; other clients: email client, FTP client; peer-to-peer has no fixed server.

qs.stem: _____ is the person who runs our web servers.
qs.sol:
In IT and web operations, job roles are distinguished by which part of the technology stack a person is responsible for — collecting and interpreting data, modeling databases, designing visual interfaces, or administering and maintaining the servers that host and serve live websites.

The person who configures, operates, and maintains a web server — publishing content, managing server settings, monitoring uptime, and keeping the hosted website running — is known as a webmaster. That is exactly the responsibility described here: the person who runs the web servers. …
qs.rel: Web roles. Neighbours: webmaster administers/maintains the site and servers; web designer = look/layout; web developer = code; DBA = database; system admin = servers/network; SEO analyst = search ranking.

qs.stem: From which of the following language is HTML derived?
qs.sol:
HTML was originally defined as an application of SGML, a standard for describing markup languages.

SGML is the markup-language standard from which early HTML was derived.
qs.rel: HTML origin. Neighbours: HTML derived from SGML (Standard Generalized Markup Language); XML is a subset of SGML; XHTML is HTML reformulated as XML; SGML DTDs defined HTML 2/4 doctypes.

qs.stem: Which of the following is a tool for site mapping and wireframing in web design?
qs.sol:
Webflow is a web design platform for arranging and prototyping website structure.

Its visual design tools can support site mapping and wireframing.
qs.rel: Wireframing tools. Neighbours: Balsamiq, Figma, Adobe XD, Sketch, Webflow, MockFlow for wireframes/prototypes; sitemap -> wireframe -> mock-up -> prototype; wireframe has no colour/typography.

qs.stem: Which of the following markup standards is commonly used for the front end of a MySQL-backed web application?
qs.sol: Modified from the official paper: the printed question asks for a frequently used front-end technology, which also admits JavaScript; the stem now specifies a markup standard. HTML 5 defines the markup structure of web pages, while JavaScript supplies behavior.
qs.rel: Front-end technology. Neighbours: HTML5 gives structure, CSS styling, JavaScript behaviour; back-end is PHP/Node/ASP with MySQL; LAMP = Linux, Apache, MySQL, PHP; AIR and ActionScript belong to Flash-era tooling.

qs.stem: Which of the following is NOT a type of INPUT element of form in HTML?
qs.sol:
HTML input supports checkbox, radio and submit types. Source is not an input type.

source is not a valid type value for input.
qs.rel: Input types. Neighbours: valid types text, password, checkbox, radio, submit, reset, button, file, hidden, email, number, date, range, color; invalid ones like textarea or select are separate tags, not input types.

qs.stem: A Java program that is embedded in an HTML document and runs in the context of a Java-capable browser is known as ______.
qs.sol: A Java program embedded in an HTML document and running within a browser context is called a Java Applet. These applications were designed to run client-side but are now largely deprecated in modern web standards.
qs.rel: Applet. Neighbours: Java applet embedded in HTML via applet/object; ran in the JVM inside browser; deprecated; servlet = server-side Java; JavaScript is unrelated to Java; canvas is HTML5 drawing surface.

qs.stem: Which of the following refers to a set of characters used to identify or name a resource on the internet?
qs.sol:
A Uniform Resource Identifier is a character string that identifies a resource on the internet.

URI identifies or names a resource.
qs.rel: URI. Neighbours: URI identifies a resource by name, location or both; URL = locator (scheme://host/path); URN = name (urn:isbn:...); every URL is a URI but not vice versa.

qs.stem: Which of the following is a standard for specifying any kind of information on the internet?
qs.sol:
A URL gives a standardized address for locating an Internet resource. The other terms concern state, page markup, or server interfaces.

A URL specifies the location of an Internet resource.
qs.rel: URL. Neighbours: URL gives address and access method (http, https, ftp, mailto, file); parts: scheme, host, port, path, query, fragment; default ports http 80, https 443.

qs.stem: Which of the following is incorrect regarding user-friendly website?

opts.A: It should have faster loading time

qs.sol: A user-friendly website should load quickly, be accessible and behave consistently across browsers. It should not be cluttered.
qs.rel: User-friendly site. Neighbours: fast load, simple navigation, consistent design, readable, responsive, accessible, clear search; slow loading, cluttered layout, broken links harm usability.

qs.stem:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are true about wire framing of website?
 I. Showing which content will appear on which page
 II. Showing navigator between pages
qs.sol:
A wireframe is the skeletal blueprint stage of UX/UI design: before any colour, typography, or imagery is decided, a wireframe deliberately strips a page down to structure — it defines WHAT content sits WHERE on a page, and HOW a user moves BETWEEN pages (the site's navigation / information architecture).

Applying this to the two statements: Statement I describes exactly the content-placement role of a wireframe — showing which content block appears on which page. Statement II describes the navigation role — showing the links/paths connecting one page to another. A standard wireframe deliverable covers both of these at the same time, so both statements hold. …
qs.rel: Wireframe. Neighbours: wireframe shows layout, content placement and navigation between pages, not colours or graphics; sitemap is page hierarchy; mock-up adds visual design; prototype adds interaction.

qs.stem: ______ produces a rough outline of what the website will look like when it is done.
qs.sol: Before visual styling and development, a designer sketches the positions of page elements and content regions. That structural outline is a wireframe. It shows the eventual page layout without requiring final colors, images, or code.
qs.rel: Wireframe outline. Neighbours: wireframe = rough outline/blueprint; mock-up = static visual design; prototype = interactive model; sitemap lists pages; storyboard shows user flow.

qs.stem: Identify the incorrect statement.

opts.B: JavaScript is the scripting standard for HTML
opts.C: DHTML is the art of combining HTML, JavaScript, DOM, and CSS
opts.D: DHTML is a term used to describe the technologies used to make web pages dynamic and interactive

qs.sol: The question asks to identify the incorrect statement regarding web technologies. Option A incorrectly defines DHTML as a programming language, whereas it is actually a combination of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Options B, C, and D accurately describe the roles of these technologies.
qs.rel: DHTML. Neighbours: DHTML = HTML+CSS+JavaScript+DOM, not a programming language; JavaScript is the scripting standard for web browsers (ECMAScript); AJAX extends dynamic behaviour.

qs.stem: Which of the following is false with reference to static website?

opts.A: Same content is loaded everytime the page is loaded
opts.B: It is loaded at a faster speed

qs.sol: Static websites serve fixed HTML files without server-side processing. Content remains consistent across visits and does not change dynamically at runtime, making the claim about runtime changes false.
qs.rel: Static website. Neighbours: static sites serve fixed files, need no server-side processing or database, are fast and cheap but content cannot be personalised; dynamic sites use DB and server scripts.

qs.stem: In client-server computing, which of the following is NOT handled by a client?
qs.sol:
A client handles its user-facing presentation and can perform local processing or storage tasks. Control of shared resources belongs to the server side of the architecture.

Shared resources are provided and controlled by the server.
qs.rel: Client duties. Neighbours: client handles user interface, input validation and display; server handles storage, business logic, authentication and DB access; thin vs thick client.

qs.stem: Which of the following actions demonstrates good netiquette in an online forum?

opts.D: Responding to others' posts with insults

qs.sol: Clear, respectful writing helps others understand a forum post. Proper grammar and punctuation are a practical part of good online etiquette.
qs.rel: Netiquette. Neighbours: be courteous, clear and concise, avoid ALL CAPS (shouting), no spam or flaming, respect privacy, quote sources; apply to email, forums and chat.

qs.stem: Which of the following is NOT an attribute of HTML LINK element used to link CSS with web pages?
qs.sol:
The link element uses href for the resource address and rel for its relationship; type can identify the media type.

“ref” is not the linking attribute shown in the question.
qs.rel: LINK attributes. Neighbours: link rel="stylesheet" href="x.css" type="text/css" media; rel, href, type, media, sizes are valid; src belongs to script/img; link is a void element in head.

qs.stem: Which statements are true about sequence structure during program execution? I. Each statement is executed once II. No statement is repeated III. The statements are executed in any order
qs.sol: Sequence control runs statements in their written order, ordinarily once each. It neither repeats a statement nor permits arbitrary execution order. Statements I and II hold; III fails.
qs.rel: Sequence structure. Neighbours: sequence = statements run once in written order; selection (if/switch) and iteration (loops) are the other two structured-programming constructs; jumps break these.

qs.stem:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
a) Front-end framework
b) Front-end asset
c) Front-end boilerplate
d) JavaScript library

List-II
i) React JS
ii) Tailwind CSS
iii) Font Awesome
iv) Reset CSS
qs.sol: Tailwind CSS is the front-end CSS framework; Font Awesome supplies front-end icons and other visual assets; Reset CSS is the front-end reset or boilerplate stylesheet; React JS is the JavaScript library. These roles give the matching Tailwind CSS → front-end framework, Font Awesome → front-end asset, Reset CSS → front-end boilerplate, and React JS → JavaScript library.
qs.rel: Front-end roles. Neighbours: framework = Tailwind/Bootstrap, library = React/jQuery, asset = Font Awesome icons/fonts/images, boilerplate = Reset CSS/Normalize/HTML5 Boilerplate; back-end = server/DB.

qs.stem: Which of the following is a web browser developed by Google?
qs.sol: Google Chrome is the browser in this list. Drive stores files, Assistant handles voice assistance, and Meet supports video meetings.

qs.stem: Which of the following networks is considered as the first network that initiated the internet ?
qs.sol: ARPANET was the early packet-switched network from which the Internet developed.

qs.stem: The protocol which provides e-mail facility is:
qs.sol: SMTP is the protocol used to submit and relay outgoing e-mail between mail systems. FTP transfers files and Telnet provides remote terminal access.

qs.stem: In 3G and 4G mobile technologies, the character ‘G’ stands for:
qs.sol:
Concept: Mobile network standards are labelled by ‘Generation’ — each numbered G (1G, 2G, 3G, 4G, 5G) marks a distinct evolutionary stage of cellular technology, standardised by bodies such as the ITU and 3GPP, each stage defined by a new radio-access technology and a step-change in data capability.

Application: 3G (third generation) introduced mobile broadband internet through UMTS/HSPA-class standards, and 4G (fourth generation) introduced LTE/LTE-Advanced, delivering all-IP high-speed data. In both ‘3G’ and ‘4G’, the character ‘G’ is short for ‘Generation’ — it is the generation-count marker attached to the numeral, not an abbreviation of any specific protocol, service, or brand. …

qs.stem: Which of the following is NOT a Web Browser?
qs.sol: JavaScript is a programming language, not a web browser. Internet Explorer, Opera, and Netscape are all established browsers.

qs.stem: Which one of the following is the most common internet protocol?
qs.sol:
The Internet is built on the TCP/IP protocol suite, with IP providing addressing and packet delivery and TCP providing a reliable transport service.

The alternatives are markup or legacy protocol suites.

qs.stem: Which of the following is not a Search Engine available over the Internet?
qs.sol:
Concept: A search engine is a software/web system that continuously crawls the internet, indexes web pages, and returns ranked results in response to a user's query -- its defining function is web-wide information retrieval on demand.

Application: Among the four options, Google Search, Bing, and Yahoo Search are each offered and used as general-purpose internet search engines: a user submits a query and receives ranked results drawn from an index of web pages (Yahoo Search's underlying results are provided through its long-running partnership with Microsoft Bing, but the service itself is still built and marketed as a search engine). …

qs.stem: What does the acronym "HTTP" stand for?
qs.sol:
Concept: Networking acronyms for internet protocols are expanded letter-by-letter into their official technical name, as fixed by the standards body (IETF) that defines the protocol. For a client-server web protocol, the expansion names (1) what kind of content it moves and (2) what action it performs on that content.

Application: Expand each letter of "HTTP" against the official specification (IETF RFC 9110, "HTTP Semantics"): H and the first T together stand for "HyperText" (linked, non-linear documents such as web pages), while the second T and P together stand for "Transfer Protocol" (the rules for moving that content between a client and a server). …

qs.stem: Which of the following is the best description of the word internet ?
qs.sol: The Internet interconnects many independent networks worldwide using common communication protocols.

qs.stem: Which protocol is used to create a secure connection between a web browser and a website so that all data is encrypted?
qs.sol: HTTPS is HTTP carried over TLS. TLS encrypts traffic between the browser and the website.

qs.stem: Which HTTP method is used for retrieving data from a server?
qs.sol:
HTTP defines a small set of standard request methods, each signalling the client's intent toward a server resource: some methods only read a resource without changing it, while others create, replace, or remove data. A method classified as safe and idempotent -- meaning it is not defined to request any change to server state, and repeating it has the same intended effect as making it once -- is the one reserved specifically for reading data.

Retrieving data from a server is exactly that read-only intent, so among the four listed methods, the one to look for is the method defined purely to fetch a resource's current representation, without requesting any creation or modification of it. …

qs.stem: Which of the following options is the correct protocol used for phone calls over the internet?
qs.sol: Carrying live voice over a packet-switched network requires digitizing the analog speech, splitting it into small IP packets, and delivering those packets with the tight timing and low latency a real conversation needs. VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol) is the umbrella technology and protocol family built around exactly this capability: the endpoints and codecs involved perform the actual digitisation and packetisation, while VoIP's signalling and transport protocols coordinate the call and carry the resulting stream. It is functionally distinct from protocols built only for link establishment, file transfer, or document retrieval. …

qs.stem: URL stands for :
qs.sol:
A Uniform Resource Locator (URL), popularly referred to as a "web address", is a structured string of characters that references a resource globally across the computer network and specifies the mechanism (protocol) to retrieve it.

As illustrated in standard networking, a typical URL is broken down into distinct functional parts:

Protocol: Specifies how data is transferred (e.g., http:// or secure https://).

Domain Name (Host): The unique name that identifies the web server hosting the asset (e.g., [www.example.com](https://www.example.com)).

Path: The specific directory routing on the server leading to the resource (e.g., /images/logo.png). …

qs.stem: Initially internet was used for ............. .
qs.sol: The Internet began as ARPANET (Advanced Research Projects Agency Network) in the late 1960s. It was funded by the U.S. Department of Defense to create a reliable network for military and research communication. Therefore, the best answer is Military Intelligence.

qs.stem: Which among the following was the first web browser?
qs.sol:
Concept: A browser's place in web history is fixed by its original public release date. Among the listed browsers, the earliest-released browser is Mosaic.

Application: Among the four listed browsers, Mosaic was released by the National Center for Supercomputing Applications (NCSA) in 1993, making it the earliest of the four. Internet Explorer followed in 1995 alongside Windows 95, Opera's development began in 1994 at a research team within the Norwegian telecom company Telenor, and Google Chrome arrived far later, in 2008. Mosaic predates all three of the other listed browsers. …

qs.stem: Which of the following is  not  a web browser?
qs.sol: A web browser is software used to access and view websites on the Internet. Mosaic, Safari, and Opera are all web browsers. MINIX, however, is an operating system, not a browser.

qs.stem: In the context of Computer Networks, the acronym TCP/IP, the T refers to :
qs.sol: TCP expands to Transmission Control Protocol, paired with Internet Protocol in TCP/IP. Therefore the initial T denotes Transmission.

qs.stem: What is the difference between a website and a web page?

opts.A: A website is a collection of web pages, while a web page is a single document that is displayed on the web.
opts.B: A website is a software program, while a web page is a hardware device.
opts.C: A website is a physical object, while a web page is a logical object.
opts.D: All of the given options are correct.

qs.sol:
A website is a collection of related web pages published together under one domain and linked through a common navigation structure, while a web page is a single document -- generally accessed through its own URL -- that a browser loads and displays. A web page is thus a unit of content; a website is the container that groups many such units together.

Applying this to the question, the description that pairs 'a collection of web pages' with 'a single document displayed on the web' captures exactly this whole-part relationship between a site and its pages, so it is the correct definition. …

qs.stem: What does IoT (Internet of Things) use to capture data from the real world?
qs.sol: Modified from the official paper: the printed stem says “To capture data from the realworld IoT uses-------”; the learner stem expands this to a grammatical question and corrects the printed “Microprocesspr” option to “Microprocessor”. ConceptAn IoT (Internet of Things) system interfaces with the physical world through two complementary classes of hardware: input devices that capture real-world data (temperature, motion, light, pressure, humidity, and so on) and output devices that act on the environment based on decisions made from that data. The input-side devices are called sensors; the output-side devices are called actuators. …

qs.sol:
DTD  stands for  Document Type Definition .

It defines the  structure, elements, and attributes  of an XML/XHTML document.

topics.deep:
- **Internet** = global network of networks using **TCP/IP**; origin: **ARPANET** funded by **ARPA** (Advanced Research Projects Agency, US Dept of Defense) from the 1960s (first link 1969). **WWW** (World Wide Web) = system of interlinked hypertext documents accessed over the Internet, invented by **Tim Berners-Lee** (CERN, 1989-91); Internet != Web (Web is one service; others: email, FTP, VoIP). Applications of the Web: e-learning, e-commerce, social media, video conferencing, online banking.
- **Key protocols:** **HTTP** (port 80) / **HTTPS** (443, TLS secure), **FTP** (20/21), **SMTP** (25, send mail), **POP3** (110) and **IMAP** (143) (receive mail), **DNS** (53, name -> IP), **DHCP** (auto IP), **BOOTP** (boots computers/diskless clients from the network; predecessor of DHCP), **Telnet** (23), **SSH** (22). IPv4 = 32-bit, IPv6 = 128-bit.
- **URL/URI:** **URI** (Uniform Resource Identifier) = string of characters identifying/naming a resource; **URL** (Locator) = URI that also gives location/access method: `scheme://host:port/path?query#fragment`; URN = name only. **Web page** (single document), **website** (collection of related web pages, entry = home page), **web server** (Apache, Nginx, IIS), **web browser** = client software (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari) that requests and renders pages, **search engine** (Google, Bing). **Webmaster** = person who runs/maintains the web servers and site; web designer designs the look; web developer codes; DBA designs databases.
- **Client-server:** client requests, server responds. Client handles presentation/user interface and input; server handles data storage, business processing, security, DB. Browser = client; web apps are often 3-tier (presentation, logic, data).
- **Static vs dynamic websites:** static = fixed HTML files served as-is, same content to all, fast, cheap, no DB; dynamic = content generated at request time from DB using server-side scripting (ASP, PHP, JSP). **DHTML** = Dynamic HTML = combination of **HTML + CSS + JavaScript + DOM**; it is not a language.
- **Web design process:** sitemap (page hierarchy) -> **wireframe** (low-fidelity blueprint: which content on which page and navigation between pages, no colours/graphics) -> mock-up -> prototype -> development. Tools: Figma, Balsamiq, Adobe XD, Webflow. **Responsive web design** (HTML + CSS, media queries, flexible grids) resizes the site to look good on all devices. **User-friendly site:** fast loading, easy navigation, consistent layout, readable fonts, mobile friendly. Front-end terms: framework (Bootstrap, Tailwind CSS), library (React JS, jQuery), asset (Font Awesome icons, images, fonts), boilerplate (Reset CSS, Normalize.css). Back-end: server, DB (MySQL), server-side language.
- **Browser features:** tabs, bookmarks, history, cache, cookies, incognito mode, extensions, **developer tools** (inspect elements, console, network; open with **F12** or **Ctrl+Shift+I** in Chrome on Windows), **geolocation** (location shared only after the user permits), pop-up blockers. Java **applet** = Java program embedded in an HTML page, run in a Java-capable browser (now deprecated).
- **Communication & netiquette:** instant messaging (WhatsApp, Telegram, WeChat, Snapchat, Signal); privacy concern = messages/personal data intercepted or stored. **Google Meet** = video conferencing (screen sharing, chat, recording, captions). **Netiquette** = respectful, clear, no ALL CAPS (shouting), no spam, stay on topic, respect privacy, cite sources.
- **Other:** email parts (To, Cc, Bcc, Subject), spam, phishing, hyperlink, hypertext, bandwidth, ISP, proxy, firewall, cookies, intranet vs extranet.
- **Likely question angles:** (1) SMTP vs POP3 vs IMAP and port numbers. (2) Parts of a URL; URL vs URI vs URN. (3) Who invented the WWW; origin of the Internet. (4) Static vs dynamic website. (5) Order wireframe, mock-up, prototype. (6) DHCP vs BOOTP vs DNS. (7) Components of DHTML. (8) Identify an IM app / browser / search engine. (9) Front-end framework vs library vs asset.
